outline: This is a history course about western classical music, which the definition, according to The New Harvard Dictionary of Music, is ”art” or ”serious” music. The styles of the various periods will be introduced from the Medieval, Renaissance, Classical, Romantic, and the Contemporary eras.
schedule:
1st week: Introduction to Western Art Music
2nd week: The Medieval Period--folk music and church music
3rd week: Renaissance--Madrigals, church music, dance music.
4th week: Renaissance--the choral music from different regions.
5th week: Baroque--Louis XIV and his influence on French music
6th week: Baroque--Italian and French legends--Corelli, Lully and Couperin
7th week: Baroque--Italian and French legends continues--Vivaldi, Scarlatti, and Rameau
8th week: Baroque--Comparison between Handel and J.S.Bach
9th week: Baroque--J.S. Bach in-depth--his string works, orchestral music, choral music, keyboard music, and Fugues.
10th week: Classical--Gluck and the history of Vienna--the form of the Viennese School and Haydn
11th week: Classical-- Mozart and Beethoven
12th week: Beethoven and the beginning of Romantic era; how Schubert was influenced by Beethoven
13th week: The pinnacle of Romantic era--Chopin, Schumann, Brahms, Liszt, Tchaikovsky
14th week: The late Romantic era--Mahler, Scriabin, and Rachmaninoff
15th week: The Contemporary Music--12-tone music (The 2nd Viennese School), Existentialism, music of Minimalism, and experimental music.
assessment:
1. Attendance
2. Learning attitude
3. Mid-term reports and Final group projects
